text.value: Most coaches, authors and influencers who tried ads got a pile of names, chased a few of them, gave up, and decided ads do not work for what they sell. Ads work fine. What went wrong happened after the person raised a hand: the message sat in an inbox until they had already bought from someone else. Once your free attention is turning into sales, we build and run the campaigns on your own Facebook and Google accounts, then answer every person who comes back in under a minute, day or night, until they book. You pay the platforms directly and see every dollar of it. What lands on your calendar is sales calls, not a list to chase.

props.intro: Paid Ads = Booked Appointments is one of six systems we build. They are designed to connect, so nobody who raises a hand gets dropped between them.

props.text: We put booked sales calls on your calendar.

That is the only thing we are trying to fill: a day of calls with people who want what you teach, chose a time, and expect you to show up. Not names to chase. Not clicks. Booked calls, on the calendar you already use.

text.label: Text: How it works
text.value: How it works

text.label: Heading: You own the accounts. We run the layer on to…
text.value: You own the accounts. We do the work on top of them.

text.label: Text: The Facebook and Google ad accounts, the piece
text.value: The Facebook and Google ad accounts, the piece of code on your website that tells Facebook and Google which ads actually turned into buyers, and the calendar are yours and stay yours. You pay the platforms directly, so you see every dollar of spend and we never touch it or mark it up. What we add is the part those platforms do not do on their own: campaigns built around what one student or client is actually worth to you, and an answer to every person the moment they raise a hand. If we ever part ways, you keep all of it and nothing switches off.

text.label: Text: It also means we report on booked appointmen…
text.value: It also means we report on sales calls on your calendar, not on how many people filled out a form. Sending more people to a website that does not sell just loses money faster, so if the follow-up is slow or the website is not turning visitors into buyers, you will hear that from us before you hear it from your bank.

props.text: What this looked like on a real account.

Riverbend Wellness & Longevity, a health and wellness clinic in San Antonio. The ads were the last thing we turned on — instant follow-up went in first, connected to the calendar, with every inquiry recorded before anyone tried to act on it. Then the traffic started.

props.body: Booked on the calendar, not inquiries. The ads brought the people in and the instant follow-up turned them into appointments — every one of them answered in seconds, day or night.
props.heading: 28 appointments in a single month

props.body: Because the follow-up never stopped. Almost nobody gets paid on week-five leads, for the simple reason that almost nobody is still talking to them.
props.heading: A week-five lead cost the same as week one

props.body: So we could prove which appointments the system produced and which the front desk booked. Most reporting cannot separate the two.
props.heading: Every booking tagged to its source

props.text: Five weeks in, the system was still holding conversations with people who inquired in week one. Nobody shows you that part, and it is the part that made the numbers hold up.
Why we turn the ads on last.

Most agencies sell you traffic on day one, because traffic is the easy part to sell and the easy part to show. But traffic arriving at a page that cannot answer it is money poured on the floor. We put the answering in place first and get your free attention selling. Then we buy more attention, and what lands on your calendar is a booked call, not a list for somebody to work through.
